content.comment_body: I am using a [product_name] with a temperature and light switching scheme. I want to adjust the offset so the temperature sensor's signal correctly reflects the actual temperature. How can I see the current reading from the temperature sensor? If I can check the sensor's signal value, I can fine-tune the offset by shifting it up or down as needed. Is it possible to read the status or value from the sensor using the messaging function or a specific parameter?
Try using the amplified input from the function modules, such as B008, B010, or B002. Alternatively, utilize the online test mode. I wish you success in finding the correct parameters.

How do I get the [product_name] to display a message? Currently, it only shows standard outputs like a1, q1, etc., marked with a black indicator. Also, how do I determine the exact value measured by the sensor to set the correct offset? I tested the sensor in water with an accurate thermometer, but regardless of the temperature, the q3 relay just toggles on and off, without showing any reliable reading. I've tried offsets of -272, -271, and also -274, -275, and -276, but none result in a true reading—the relays switch on and off every few minutes. Even with the online test mode on the PC, I still can't get a precise sensor measurement (for example, it shows 300, which I expect to correspond to 27°C, but my thermometer says 25°C, so the offset adjustment is unclear).

Please consult the manual. As another user mentioned on the German-language page, you need to connect a message text to a 'high' signal. Without doing so, nothing is displayed. You must click the message text twice and then select which parameter to show—the same parameters previously explained. Regarding the offset problem: It might help if you specify the sensor you're using and the signal type it produces. It appears it is not a PT100; that would be very straightforward.

I am not sure which sensor I have, as I purchased it from an online seller ([user_name]) and have not yet received a response about its specifications. The sensor seems unreliable, so I am considering using an LM35 or LM335 and assembling it myself. Initially, I bought this sensor because I was unsure how to implement an LM35, but now I plan to buy either an LM35 or LM335.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing difficulties calibrating and obtaining accurate temperature readings when using the [product_name] with their sensors. There is confusion about how to monitor real-time sensor data, configure display messages, and apply correct offsets. Uncertainty regarding sensor type and lack of reliable feedback from the device's interface increases user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to access real-time and accurate temperature readings from their sensor via the [product_name] display, with simple options for fine-tuning offset values for precise measurements. They also hope for clear interface features to reliably display actual measured sensor values and consistent relay operation.
